bibliography.title: SVRG and Beyond via Posterior Correction

sections.title: C. Derivation of the Newton-like SVRG Extension
D. Derivation of the Adam-like SVRG Extension

abstract_sentences.text: Stochastic Variance Reduced Gradient (SVRG) and its variants aim to speed-up training by using gradient corrections.
Originally proposed over a decade ago, these methods have never been connected to any Bayesian method at a fundamental level.
Here, we fill this gap and derive surprising new connections of SVRG to a recently proposed Bayesian method called ‘posterior correction’.
Our main contribution is to show that SVRG can be recovered as a special case of posterior-correction over isotropic-Gaussian posteriors.
Novel extensions of SVRG are automatically obtained by using more flexible exponential-family posteriors.
We derive two new such extensions by using Gaussian families: a Newton-like variant with novel Hessian corrections, and an Adam-like extension that scales to large problems.
Our work is the first to connect SVRG to Bayes and use it to speed-up training.

claim_closure.claim: SVRG is a special case of posterior correction.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. 16-18, Theorem 1-2 and Algorithm 3 derive the correspondence.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 3 gives a VSGD/VSGD-PoCo empirical analogue.

claim_closure.claim: Posterior correction can generate extensions beyond existing SVRG variants.
claim_closure.method_response: Full and diagonal Gaussian choices yield Newton-like and IVON-like algorithms.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Convex and deep-learning experiments instantiate these choices, but not arbitrary exponential families.

claim_closure.claim: Hessian correction is the Newton-like novelty.
claim_closure.method_response: Theorem 3 and Eq. 19-20 derive a corrected precision/Hessian update.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 2 compares IVON with IVON-PoCo, without a deletion ablation that isolates the Hessian term.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion groups the result under new algorithms.

claim_closure.claim: IVON-PoCo scales to large deep-learning problems.
claim_closure.method_response: Algorithm 4 uses diagonal Gaussian state and mega-batches with O(d) storage discussion.
claim_closure.evidence_response: GPT-2, ImageNet, continual-pretraining and finetuning are tested; efficiency depends on the denominator.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion limits the claimed deep-learning speed-up.

evidence.anchor: do not yet provide similar speed-ups

claim_closure.claim: The connection can speed up deep-learning training.
claim_closure.method_response: The methods add corrections and mega-batch estimates.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Final quality can improve, while p9 reports no tangible speed-ups under gradient-computation accounting.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Future work is explicitly invited to boost deep learning.

rhetoric_analysis.interpretation: The domain nouns are mechanism-bearing; author-voice verbs cluster in theory and result interpretation.

final_judgment.single_storyline: PoCo treats old posterior sites as transferable knowledge; in natural-gradient space this recovers SVRG and generates Hessian-corrected and IVON-like variants through posterior-family choices.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps the ERM-to-BLR-to-PoCo derivation, Algorithms 1-4, Theorems 1-3, convex task curves, GPT-2/ImageNet counter-accounting, and the conclusion's deep-learning limit.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: The appendix moves detailed algebra, proof steps, Algorithm 5, extra tasks, alpha/refresh sensitivity, hyperparameters, hardware and data-split details; this preserves conceptual readability but means proof and full reproduction require the appendix.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1's isomorphic pseudocode visualizes the theta/gradient to lambda/natural-gradient mapping before the theorems; Figure 5 then evaluates the same claim under two resource denominators.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Deep-learning quality improvements are shown, while repeat-level uncertainty is unreported and general speed-up under data or gradient accounting remains open.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a claimed generalization, connect exact special-case equivalence, the newly added state, executable algorithms, and outcomes under more than one resource denominator.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule suits optimization papers with explicit updates and controlled compute accounting; it cannot replace replication statistics, deployment evidence, or exhaustive literature-priority verification.
